positioning: The elegant guardian with a tender streak.
story: The Doberman Pinscher looks like a statue and acts like a shadow. Every muscle is polished. Every glance is on you.
Louis Dobermann, a tax collector in Apolda, Germany, created the breed in the 1890s. He wanted a loyal, fearless dog to walk beside him on his rounds. The exact recipe was never written down.
The result was fast, strong, and smart. After Dobermann died in 1894, breeders refined the dog into the sleek athlete we know. The AKC recognized the breed in 1908.
In World War II, the U.S. Marines used Dobermans as scouts and messengers in the Pacific, most famously on Guam in 1944. A war dog memorial there honors the dogs that died.
At home, a Doberman is not the villain of the movies. It is affectionate, eager, and clingy. It leans on you, stares at you, and waits for the next job.
Give it training, exercise, and respect, and it will protect you for life. Even in a pool noodle, it keeps its dignity.
fblocks: Named for Louis Dobermann, the German tax collector who created the breed. Pinscher is German for a terrier type.
Kurt, a Marine war dog honored on Guam. Dobermans also serve as police and search dogs.
Heart disease occurs, so choose a screened breeder. Needs daily exercise and steady training. Hates being left alone.
A short, sleek coat in black, red, blue, or fawn, with rust markings.
Sixty to one hundred pounds. Created in the 1890s. Recognized by the AKC in 1908.

last_walk:
The lake turns copper, and the last light of summer fades.
Titan walks the lakeside road with old Duchess. He matches her pace. She leans, just a little, on his shoulder. A Doberman is a guardian all day. At dusk it is a friend. The first leaf drops, and neither dog looks up.
